SRC-250:R001.text: Continue the existing authorized SAIPEN mission non-disruptively: do not interrupt the active ticket, override ownership, bypass admission or create a new meta-project; integrate these principles into admitted work

SRC-250:R002.text: Correctness before speed: prioritize root causes of unauthorized transitions, state or journal corruption, concurrent overwrites, lost or duplicated work, recovery deadlocks, contradictory instructions, false success, stale or fabricated evidence, unsafe identity handling, needless operator intervention and state/behaviour divergence; remove whole failure classes; never weaken security, provenance, ownership or forensic integrity for throughput

SRC-250:R003.text: Establish a lightweight reproducible protocol-cost baseline from existing logs, tests and lifecycle evidence (lifecycle duration, engineering versus administration, validation time, repeated attempts, recoveries, manual actions, repeated validation, duplicates, blockers, completion rate, complexity delta), separating elapsed time from work and ticket classes, without a new telemetry subsystem

SRC-250:R004.text: Every meaningful correction justifies its complexity: the failure class it eliminates, the owning mechanism, no new competing authority, no new mandatory ordinary step, no unexpiring fallback, no needless persistent metadata, reuse before new code, simplification where safe

SRC-250:R005.text: Keep the cold path small (BOOT, continue --json, phase file); optional machinery stays off the ordinary path; a weaker model follows the ordinary path deterministically

SRC-250:R006.text: Self-healing without false authority: bounded canonical repair of recoverable conditions the protocol already authorizes, resuming the original request idempotently; never auto-repair untrusted provenance, foreign ownership, missing privileged authorization, unadmitted forensic corruption, ambiguous destructive operations, conflicting identities or missing cutover approval; bounded failures end with a terminal reason

SRC-250:R007.text: Make completion complete: investigate Work DONE with ACTIVE receipts, passing verification with blocked completion, continue recommending what claim rejects, redundant manual reconciliation, dry runs mistaken for execution and recoveries leaving unexplained work; where evidence and authority exist make canonical completion deterministic, never inventing evidence or closing unresolved audit requirements

SRC-250:R008.text: Maintain a small representative acceptance matrix (clean continuation, cold start, interrupted resume, recoverable stale evidence, unauthorized or foreign refusal, completion with source reconciliation, Windows managed-account execution, concurrent access without lost updates) with real host verification where required; no simulation reported as acceptance

SRC-250:R009.text: Maintenance economics: weigh observed current cost, expected benefit and implementation cost; no invented savings; expensive corrections only for significant recurring failure classes

SRC-250:R010.text: No unnecessary framework growth: no new orchestration frameworks, parallel authorities, unexpiring compatibility paths, duplicate registries, redundant lifecycle states, unbounded self-repair or long-lived metadata for transient observations; simplify while correcting; remove obsolete behaviour only with proof

SRC-250:R011.text: Weaker-model acceptance: concise structured machine-readable answers with one exact next action; diagnostics available without flooding the ordinary agent

SRC-250:R012.text: Protect cross-project boundaries: SAIPEN owns protocol, engine, runtime and recovery policy; SAITULS and AUDAPACK keep independent admission and ownership; no target-project modification on SAIPEN admission alone; the corrupt AUDAPACK lineage is never modified

SRC-250:R013.text: After each significant correction record concise evidence of the root cause eliminated, regression coverage, workflow improvement, administrative steps removed or added, remaining risks and complexity delta in existing evidence; compare periodically against the baseline

SRC-250:R014.text: Stop and escalation: continue autonomously within verified authority; ask the operator only for genuine decisions or permissions; stop the affected operation on missing admission, foreign ownership, untrusted provenance, unsafe destruction, unresolved forensic corruption, required privileged approval, repeated ineffective recovery or a correction that cannot pass real acceptance

SRC-250:R015.text: Definition of success and final direction: boringly reliable SAIPEN, exact next actions, canonical recovery, safe refusals, trustworthy evidence, automatic reconciliation, correct resume, model-independent correctness, rare operator intervention, measurable payoff of each architectural investment
